fact: The telecom union FESATEL's secretary general said on 21 May 2026 that Starlink is not recognised in Guinea today and Wifi-Zone operators must not use Starlink equipment to provide internet.

Agence Ecofin reported on 31 August 2026 that Guinea is among 16 countries marked 'Starting in 2026' on Starlink's availability map, meaning coverage or regulatory authorisation pending, and that Starlink service is still not available there despite a 2025 target.
Guinea's regulator ARPT stated in a communique of 30 March 2026 that users may not sell Wi-Fi supplied over Starlink in 'Wi-Fi zones', no licence or prior authorisation having been issued.
ARPT agents were sent into the field to uninstall and confiscate Starlink equipment used by Wi-Fi resellers in Guinea, as reported on 10 August 2026 (date of the seizures not given).
MyBroadband's 17 July 2026 table of Starlink status lists Guinea with estimated availability '2026', not 'Available', so no Starlink service was on sale in Guinea.
TechnoMag's mid-2026 table lists Guinea among countries where Starlink is 'scheduled for 2026', not among those active now.
